title: Footings below the frost line
requirement: Every deck footing must extend below the local frost depth, and not less than 12 in below undisturbed grade, so frost heave cannot lift the deck.

title: Footing size from the post load
requirement: A deck footing is at least 12 in in diameter and large enough that the post load divided by the soil bearing capacity stays inside the pad.

title: Allowable soil bearing
requirement: Use an allowable bearing pressure from a soil test or the code table: 2,000 psf is the usual assumed default, 1,500 psf for clay and 3,000 psf for compact sand or gravel.

title: Joist size and span
requirement: Deck joists are sized from the span and spacing: 40 psf live load, L/360 live deflection, and the species and grade stamped on the lumber.

title: Joist spacing matched to the decking
requirement: Joist spacing may not exceed the decking’s listed span: typically 16 in for 5/4 boards, 24 in for 2x6, and often 12 in for composite laid diagonally.

title: Built-up beam spans
requirement: A deck beam carries half of each joist span and is sized from the post spacing; plies are nailed or bolted together so they act as one member.

title: Post size and height
requirement: Deck posts are sized for the load and height: 6x6 for beam posts on most decks, with 4x4 limited to low, lightly loaded decks and bracing added as height grows.

title: Post bases and caps
requirement: A post must be connected to its footing and to the beam so uplift and lateral load cannot separate them, and it must be held above the concrete to shed water.

title: Attaching the ledger to the house
requirement: A ledger is attached with 1/2 in lag screws or bolts in two rows, staggered, spaced per the table for the joist span, with the band joist checked for the added load.

title: Ledger flashing and water management
requirement: The ledger needs flashed top and bottom, with a water-resistive barrier lapped over the flashing and a gap or spacer so water cannot sit against the house.

title: Lateral restraint for the deck
requirement: A ledger-attached deck needs lateral ties or an equivalent connection so the deck cannot pull away from the house: at least two tension ties, or a designed frame.

title: Board span and layout
requirement: Decking boards span no further than the manufacturer allows between joists, and the layout accounts for the gap, the end joints and the pattern.

title: Board gaps and drainage
requirement: Leave a gap between boards so water drains and debris cannot trap moisture: about 1/8–1/4 in for wood, and the manufacturer’s gap for composite and PVC.

title: Fasteners and corrosion
requirement: Use two fasteners per board at every joist, in stainless or coated steel compatible with the treatment, and hidden clips where the board calls for them.

title: When a guard is required
requirement: A deck more than 30 in above the grade or floor below needs a guard on every open side, including the stair opening.

title: Guard height 36 in
requirement: The guard is at least 36 in high measured vertically from the deck surface, on the open sides of a one- and two-family dwelling.

title: The 4 in sphere rule
requirement: No opening in a guard may pass a 4 in sphere, and the triangle formed by the stair tread, riser and guard may not pass a 6 in sphere.

title: Guard posts and their connection
requirement: Guard posts are spaced no more than about 6 ft on center and are bolted or through-bolted to the rim or blocked framing, so a 200 lb push does not lever them loose.

title: Riser height 7¾ in maximum
requirement: Every riser is 7¾ in (196 mm) or less, and all risers in a flight are within 3/8 in of each other.

title: Tread depth 10 in minimum
requirement: Treads are at least 10 in (254 mm) deep, with a nosing of ¾–1¼ in where the tread does not project over the riser.

title: Stair width and headroom
requirement: A stair is at least 36 in (914 mm) clear width above the handrail height, with 6 ft 8 in (2032 mm) of headroom measured vertically.

title: Handrails 34–38 in
requirement: A stair of four or more risers needs a graspable handrail 34–38 in above the tread nosing, continuous for the flight, with 1½ in clearance from the wall.

title: Stringers and their bearing
requirement: Outdoor stairs use 2x12 stringers, not more than 36 in apart, bearing on a footing or the deck frame and connected at both ends.

title: Decay-resistant framing near grade
requirement: Wood within 6 in of grade, in contact with concrete, or exposed to weather must be naturally durable or pressure treated for ground contact and cut ends field-treated.

title: Drainage and grade below the deck
requirement: The ground below the deck falls away from the house, and the deck surface sheds water through the board gaps or a drainage system.

title: Airflow under the deck
requirement: Leave 18 in or more of clear space under the joists for airflow, or ventilate a skirted deck, so the framing can dry after rain.

title: Setbacks and lot coverage
requirement: Decks, stairs and footings must respect the side, rear and front setbacks, easements and the lot’s impervious-cover limit.

title: What the inspector needs
requirement: A dimensioned framing plan, the footing and post schedule, the ledger attachment detail, the guard and stair details, and the fastener and connector listing.
